newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Reuters foreign exchange poll - Dec.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Reuters foreign exchange poll - Dec.

text.p: The dollar is expected to remain close to current levels against the mark over the next month according to a Reuter poll of 35 banks and financial institutions across the globe.

At 1200 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.5603/10 marks and 112.66/76 yen. Sterling/dollar was quoted at $1.6240/50, sterling/mark at 2.5305/15 and mark/yen at 72.25/27.
The minimum and maximum forecasts were as follows --
On average the forecasters polled expect dollar/mark to be trading at 1.5582 one month from now, before rising to 1.5530 in six months.
The dollar is expected to trade at 1.5459 marks in a year from now. The lowest dollar/mark is expected to fall during this period is 1.4200, the highest it is likely to rise is 1.7000.
The dollar is expected to slip against the yen before the end of 1996 and continue a gradual decline throughout the following twelve months.

In one month's time it is seen at 112.45 yen, slipping to 111.15 yen in six months before tailing off to 109.79 in a year's time. The highest forecast for dollar/yen during this period is 120.00 yen, the lowest 98.00.

The poll showed sterling will make some gains during the next month. In three months time it is expected to stand at $1.6493 before weakening to $1.6425 in six months. It is then expected to pick up slightly and finish 1997 at $1.6445.
The lowest level sterling is expected to fall to is $1.4700, the highest level is $1.9000 in a year from now.
Rankings of the 35 forecasters by the accuracy of their one-month forecasts will be published in the first week of January, just before the results of the next poll.
